doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sinatra, Shirley Horn and film songs
title: The Americanization of Emily and the start of songwriting
summary: After vocal albums and the Andy Williams show, Mandel got a Filmways picture that let him write his first song of consequence.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Of course. Well speaking of The Sandpiper, why don’t we jump back to say the early 60s.
Or, in fairness that you said after you’d done, I Want to Live! you had done TV writing you had done a couple of, B movies.
I did a lot of vocal albums.

And really… then did the Andy Williams, I was gonna say Andy Warhol, Andy Williams and right after the Andy Williams thing, I really got connected up with Filmways [Production Company] and got a shot to do The Americanization of Emily, a very good picture, a

chance to write a song, something I hadn't foreseen. And my first song of any consequence, even though when I look back now I had written songs that could've been songs. But I never thought of myself as a songwriter.
“Just a Child,” goes under that category doesn’t it?
Yeah, and stuff from, I Want to Live!, “Barbara’s theme,” you know several themes in that could've taken lyrics.
“Black Nightgown,” a lot of those could’ve taken lyrics.
